metrics.storage_scope: diagnostic per-tensor quantized payload plus codec metadata; checkpoint is lossless RGBD FP32
metrics.memory_method: process RSS sampled at 10 ms; CUDA allocator peak if available

execution.training_method: fake quantization with identity straight-through gradients
limitations: Dense, embedding, normalization, nonlinearities, softmax, and gradient kernels use floating point.
Master parameters and optimizer states stay floating point; estimated code bytes are not measured training-memory savings.
Chromatic uniform palettes relabel the same scalar levels as equal-bit uniform integer quantization.
Straight-through gradients approximate discrete assignment, rounding, and clipping.

checkpoint_probe.source: first real held-out inputs from the recorded dataset
checkpoint_probe.scope: CPU checkpoint replay only; original task accuracy, precision and timings are unchanged

operation_estimate.convention: two multiply/add operations per matrix-product term, including products at causally masked positions
operation_estimate.scope: one inference batch; excludes rounding, RGB packing, scale estimation, clipping, gathers, nearest-code norms/argmin, bias, activations, normalization, softmax, memory traffic and backward
operation_estimate.training_scope: codebook-attention training additionally computes a QK gradient surrogate; inference estimates exclude it

storage_accounting.scope: last captured quantizer states; RGB byte triples retain duplicate integer IDs for inspection; overlapping layer inputs and outputs are counted separately
storage_accounting.checkpoint_format: lossless RGBD storage of FP32 master values plus integer buffers
storage_accounting.byte_ledger_note: chroma8 has 8-bit scalar levels but fake forward stores one three-byte RGB symbol per encoded scalar; live FP32 parameters and inspection buffers remain allocated

conclusions: Quantization-aware networks use floating point master parameters, optimizer state, matrix products, normalization, and softmax. The operator lookup and grid-add paths perform integer operations after their tables or scale metadata have been prepared.

The executed profile is a seeded research pilot. Limited training, small models, and two seeds do not establish state-of-the-art accuracy, novel mathematics, end-to-end integer training, or a general speed advantage.

instrumentation.analytic_estimates: one recorded inference batch, matrix products only

profiler_runs.source: one torch.profiler forward of the trained checksum-validated checkpoint
profiler_runs.sample_source: deterministic synthetic linspace inputs; this is operation evidence, not another accuracy evaluation

runtime_storage_on_this_batch.scope: last captured quantizer states; RGB byte triples retain duplicate integer IDs for inspection; overlapping layer inputs and outputs are counted separately

limits: Profiler FLOP annotations cover selected operators, not every instruction or tensor operation.
No backward pass, optimizer, GPU kernel, or end-to-end training run was profiled.
Profiler CPU times include profiling overhead and are not used as benchmark latency.
Nominal quantization bits are separate from physical RGB storage and live training memory.
Matrix FLOP estimates and profiler annotations are partial arithmetic accounts, not exact hardware counts.
Checkpoint validation recovers trained master values; profiling uses synthetic CPU inputs and does not replace the recorded validation metrics.

public_sanitization.changes: Machine paths redacted; numbers, seeds, sample counts and execution precision preserved. Missing companion data and old source hashes cannot certify this release.
